### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db1f1fd20fba543408b209746e566b48373a4622`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db1f1fd20fba543408b209746e566b48373a4622` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3c3042956018156df114ffc9e7efcd6e3e19d32d` — the merge of head `83425d5bc1cb39855f7f991131b7d0d8d3c60e69` into base `db1f1fd20fba543408b209746e566b48373a4622`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3c3042956018156df114ffc9e7efcd6e3e19d32d && git checkout 3c3042956018156df114ffc9e7efcd6e3e19d32d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin db1f1fd20fba543408b209746e566b48373a4622 83425d5bc1cb39855f7f991131b7d0d8d3c60e69 && git checkout -B drift-repro db1f1fd20fba543408b209746e566b48373a4622 && git merge --no-ff 83425d5bc1cb39855f7f991131b7d0d8d3c60e69

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db1f1fd20fba543408b209746e566b48373a4622
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs db1f1fd20fba543408b209746e566b48373a4622` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Who skips (item 1) — right.** `importUndoWriteContext` (`data-action-routes.ts`, new, called once at the undo route) spreads the resolved caller context and adds `skipAutomations: true, skipStateMachine: true` only when `isSystem === true`, read as `(context as { isSystem?: unknown } | null | undefined)?.isSystem === true` — byte-for-byte the predicate `importControlOptOutRefusal` asks at `import-prepare.ts:285` (`741aa85da`). `rest-server.ts` states twice that `isSystem` is never set on inbound HTTP, and at this head it carries no spelling of `skipAutomations`, `skipStateMachine`, `preserveAudit` or `seedReplay`, so no HTTP caller can carry a skip in through the spread. 2. **A refused row (item 2) — right.** Each reversal is tried per row; a throw pushes `{ id, action, code, error }` onto `failures` and the row onto `unreverted` (the created id, or the updated `{ id, before }` snapshot). `deleted` / `restored` count successes only, `failed` is `failures.length`, `success` is `failures.length === 0`. `reverted_at` is written only when `failures` is empty; otherwise the job row's `undo_log` is rewritten to `{ created: the unreverted ids, updated: the unreverted snapshots, failures }` and nothing is stamped. `parseUndoLog` (`rest-server.ts:944`) reads `created` and `updated` only and tolerates the extra key; `importJobUndoable` is true while that log is non-empty and `reverted_at` is unset. So a retry reads exactly the rows that remain and never one already reverted, and `GET /import/jobs/:jobId` keeps answering `undoable: true` with no `revertedAt`. Pinned: test 3 (one refused restore, the stored log, the retry reverting only that row and stamping), test 4 (a refused delete and a refused restore, both kept). The ruling's "the job's history" is met by the stored row; see ③ for what the progress route does not project.

3. **Withholding — right.** `importUndoFailure` classifies with `mapDataError` (`packages/types`, the classification `PATCH` / `DELETE /data/:object/:id` use): a sandboxed hook's refusal answers its `innerMessage` sentence, a validation rule its `VALIDATION_FAILED` message, and anything unclassified lands in `UNCLASSIFIED_FAULT` — `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` with the fixed sentence and no driver text. `nestedRefusalEnvelope` fills `code` from the catalog's floor when the classification declared none, so `code` is always a string as the schema requires, and `message` is the classified body's `error`. `logUnexpectedRouteError(error, mapped)` logs a genuine fault once, as those doors do. Pinned: `VALIDATION_ERROR` with the hook's own sentence (test 4), `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the rule's message (test 3). The fault arm has no pin of its own here; the classification is the shared one and its own tests hold it.

4. **`preserveAudit` (item 3) — unchanged, right.** `job.treat_as_historical ? { preserveAudit: true } : {}` for every caller, beside the skips for the system principal and alone for everyone else. Pinned both ways (tests 5, 6, on the contexts the protocol actually received).

- **`@objectstack/rest` changeset — right.** `minor`, `fix(rest)!:`, line-initial `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, exactly one marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a `**BREAKING**` sentence naming the cost the ruling names and the remedy. `741aa85da`'s shape, and what the diff publishes: fewer controls taken off the writes, plus the answer's new key and the changed meaning of `success` and `reverted_at`. The marker's category holds: nothing an author writes moves, the undo log stays an engine-owned json column, no arrow-bearing prescription in the body.
- **PR body — right.** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, line-initial, with its basis. Both moved packages are graded `minor`, so the level axis reads clean (`Check Changeset` green on both runs).
- **`@objectstack/spec` changeset — wrong arm.** It reads `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, no `**BREAKING**`, no marker, no `!`, with the basis that spec "narrows nothing". `UndoImportJobResponseSchema` gains a REQUIRED key: at the merge base `UndoImportJobResponseSchema.parse` accepted an undo answer without `failures`, at this head it refuses one (the PR's own test 3 parses with `.strict()`), and any code that constructs a `UndoImportJobResponse` must now supply it. The PR body's line stays as it is. The alternative, `.optional()` on `failures` keeping `yes (widening)`, weakens the contract against the `hasMore` precedent and is not recommended.
